originalTitle: Sharp objects found in Halloween sweets in three European nations
summary: Dozens of cases are reported in Austria, Germany and Hungary, including a nine-year-old girl hurting her tongue while eating chocolate containing a pin.
content:
Needles and other sharp metal objects have been found in sweets handed out over Halloween in Germany, Austria and Hungary, prompting police to issue warnings to parents to check what their children have been given.

Police in a number of German states have reported cases, from Bavaria in the south-east to Lower Saxony in the north.

A girl aged nine hurt her tongue while eating a chocolate bar in Bremervörde, west of Hamburg. A 5cm-long (2in) pin was then found inside it.

Meanwhile, police in Hungary have launched a criminal investigation after nails, screws and pieces of wire were found in sweets handed out to children who had been trick-or-treating in and around the town of Gyömrő, to the east of Budapest.

The local authority said one young girl had been handed a toffee with a nail inside a chocolate wrapper and that she had fortunately noticed in time and had not swallowed the sweet.

Several cases have also been reported across Austria, where Interior Minister Gerhard Karner condemned the incidents as "cowardly, malicious and in some cases life-threatening".

A chocolate wrapper was used to hand a girl a toffee with a sharp tack inside it in Hungary

Police there said investigations were under way in four states, and that a 10-year-old girl had suffered a minor injury to her mouth when she bit into a small chocolate bar in the Amstetten area to the east of Linz.

Lower Austria Governor Johanna Mikl-Leitner said the perpetrators had to feel the full force of the law, adding: "Our children deserve a carefree childhood and we'll continue to ensure that."

Warning after 'metal pins' found in Halloween sweets

German police in the south-eastern state of Bavaria said that, while there had been similar cases reported in the past two years, initial figures this year suggested a significant increase in incidents.

As many as 25 cases involving sweets containing needles, screws or nails have been reported by police in Bavaria.

Police in the Middle Franconia region of western Bavaria have also warned of the risk of copycat actions, after a mother found a needle in her child's chocolate bar and reported it to police.

She later returned to the police to say her child had admitted to inserting the needle.

chineseTitle: 三个欧洲国家的万圣节糖果中发现尖锐物体
chineseSummary: 奥地利、德国和匈牙利报告了数十起病例，其中包括一名九岁女孩在吃含有别针的巧克力时弄伤了舌头。
chineseContent:
德国、奥地利和匈牙利万圣节期间分发的糖果中发现了针头和其他锋利的金属物体，促使警方向家长发出警告，检查他们的孩子收到的糖果。

从东南部的巴伐利亚到北部的下萨克森州，德国许多州的警方都报告了案件。

在汉堡西部的 Bremervörde，一名九岁的女孩在吃巧克力棒时弄伤了舌头。然后在里面发现了一根 5 厘米（2 英寸）长的别针。

与此同时，匈牙利警方在布达佩斯东部杰姆鲁镇及周边地区向那些曾玩过“不给糖就捣蛋”的儿童发放的糖果中发现了钉子、螺丝和金属丝，并展开了刑事调查。

当地政府表示，有人递给一名年轻女孩一颗巧克力包装纸内有钉子的太妃糖，幸运的是她及时注意到，没有吞下这颗糖。

奥地利各地也报告了几起案件，内政部长格哈德·卡纳谴责这些事件“懦弱、恶意，在某些情况下危及生命”。

在匈牙利，一个女孩用巧克力包装纸递给一个里面有锋利的大头钉的太妃糖

当地警方表示，四个州正在进行调查，一名 10 岁女孩在林茨东部的阿姆施泰滕地区咬了一块小巧克力，导致嘴部受轻伤。

下奥地利州州长约翰娜·米克尔·莱特纳 (Johanna Mikl-Leitner) 表示，肇事者必须感受到法律的全部效力，并补充道：“我们的孩子应该拥有无忧无虑的童年，我们将继续确保这一点。”

万圣节糖果中发现“金属别针”后发出警告

德国东南部巴伐利亚州警方表示，虽然过去两年曾报告过类似案件，但今年的初步数据显示，此类案件数量大幅增加。

巴伐利亚州警方已报告多达 25 起涉及含有针、螺丝或钉子的糖果的案件。

巴伐利亚州西部中弗兰肯地区的警方也警告称，在一名母亲在孩子的巧克力棒中发现一根针并向警方报告后，可能会出现模仿行为。

她后来向警方表示，她的孩子承认插过针。
